notes: Rn-222 only. source_ids lists S0001 (UNSCEAR 2016 para 111 quotes the S0242/S0247 coefficients); primary sources S0203 (TRS 474), S0242 (Sakoda), S0247 (Solecki), also cited here. Fly ash: emanation coefficients Sakoda 0.03 (S0242), Solecki 0.08-0.13 (S0247), TRS 474 <0.1 (S0203); low 0.005 is the Phase 1 proposal (research/coal/notes.md), untraced. Emanation coefficient used as effective exhalation fraction (not the same quantity). Rn-220 left empty: no Phase 1 value (BLOCKER, see research/coal/factors_notes.md). Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): Generic Kd-retardation flush M1 (I 7-100 mm/a, H 4-15 m, rho_b 1000-1600 kg/m3, theta 0.35, Kd Ra 71-2500 L/kg), log-uniform Monte Carlo P5/P50/P95 = 6.9e-7 / 6.4e-6 / 5.9e-5. No direct ash-pond radionuclide measurement found. Almahayni (S0950) Kd are 10% of the geometric mean (conservative); implied Ra s from its leachate maxima 2.6e-7 to 2.4e-4 per a (thin 0.3 m layer). U would be about 30x higher, Pb-210 about 5x lower (notes section 4). Alkaline ash (pH above 8) lowers U Kd (S0955) and raises U share.

Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): M4: s = I C_sat /(H rho_b), C_sat 2.5-3.1 kg/m3 gypsum (S0964), rho_b 900-1200 kg/m3, gives P5/P50/P95 2.3e-6 / 9.3e-6 / 3.8e-5 assuming Ra releases congruently with Ca (upper limit; Ra re-uptake by barite lowers it). Low set to the M1 sorption-limited P5. Covers wet-stack and landfilled gypsum only; gypsum in wallboard is Dispersed. Dry-scrubber (CaSO3) and FBC residues not covered.

description: Coal washery refuse and above-threshold mine waste
notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): S0225: Piast colliery waste rock, Ra-226 83 Bq/kg, leachate below 0.1 Bq/L at L/S 10, so fraction leached at most 1.2% per 10 L/kg; times L/S per year 0.0027 gives at most 3.2e-6 per a at the median hydrology. High keeps the M1 P95 as an allowance for sulphide oxidation and sulphate depletion, which the test did not simulate (Elliot Lake behaviour, S0957).

description: Radium-bearing sludge from coal mine water treatment
notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): S0225 batch tests at L/S 10 with 10 g/L NaCl: Ba-carrier deposits (type A) release 0.004% of Ra; adsorbed-Ra sediments without Ba (type B) 5-7%; type A about three orders lower than B. Triple spans A (low, M2 P5) to B (high, M2 P95 7e-5); central = geometric mean of the A and B medians (1.1e-8, 1.6e-5), because the sludge mix is unknown. BaCl2-treated sludge is type A; settling-pond sediment is type B.

description: Ash from residential and small-scale coal burning
notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade D): Household ash is largely Dispersed; the impounded part sits in municipal landfills with higher leachate generation than assumed here, which is not quantified. Cross-check: raw municipal-landfill leachate Ra 0.116 Bq/L mean (S0967) is compatible (notes section 6).

Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): Barite scale: 0.11% of Ra leached at L/S about 55 L/kg (S0961, upper value for sludge) and 0.004% at L/S 10 (type A, S0225) correspond to 4e-6 to 2e-5 per L/kg; times L/S per year 0.0027 gives 1e-8 to 5e-8. High = soil-incubation result 0.36% at L/S about 9 (4e-4 per L/kg) times P95 hydrology = 4.4e-6, about the Elliot Lake barite-dissolution rate. Calcium-sulfate or carbonate-hosted Ra is more soluble (S0971, qualitative) and not covered.

description: Oil and gas sludge (tanks, pits, land-farmed)
notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): Tank sludge was the most leachable sample in S0961 (0.11% at L/S about 55). Same high as og_scale. Oil-coated particles biodegrade and sludge is often land-farmed (Dispersed, not here), so release may rise as hydrocarbons degrade; not quantified.

description: Rare-earth processing residues (cracking, leaching, solvent extraction)

notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): Same M1 triple as ree_tailings; S0963 shows negligible Th release over 12 months in seawater, supporting the lower half. description: Base- and precious-metal mine tailings (Cu, Zn, Pb, Ag, Ni and others)
notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade D): Defensible only for sulphide-bearing hard-rock tailings where Ra is controlled by (Ra,Ba)SO4 as at Elliot Lake; no Cu, Zn, Pb or Ni tailings radionuclide-seepage measurement was found. K-40 and Th-232 in silicate gangue are effectively immobile on this scale (no data).

Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade D): Oxide gangue, near-neutral, no sulphide control; generic M1 only. No iron-ore tailings radionuclide data found. Activity is low and dominated by K-40 and Th-232 held in silicates (no seepage data).

notes: Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade C): K in wood ash is largely soluble salts, so it is flush-limited not Kd-limited: I/(H theta) P5/P50/P95 = 2.4e-3 / 9.8e-3 / 3.9e-2. Supports: loose field ash lost 50-60% of K within a year (S0965; not impounded). Wood-ash natural nuclides are a memo series under D44; this triple matters only where the stream treats ash K-40 as counted. Ra226+ would take the fly-ash triple.

Seepage (modelled, research/seepage/notes.md, grade D): Peat is a flow under D44; its ash is mineral-rich and similar in hydrology to coal ash. No peat-ash leaching data found. K-40 in peat ash is likely soluble (use the biomass_ash K triple for that group).
